Step 05 - Standardize spelling

Source: vignettes/step-05-standardize-spelling.Rmd
step-05-standardize-spelling.Rmd

The dictionary layer. standardize_spelling() expands abbreviations, fixes common misspellings and truncations, and writes each kind of title one way, so that the crosswalk in step 07 needs one entry per title rather than one per spelling.

Before and after

before (TitleTxt4) after (TitleTxt5)
EXEC DIR EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR
SEC SECRETARY
TREAS TREASURER
ASST SECRETARY ASSISTANT SECRETARY
DIR OF DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR OF DEVELOPMENT
DIR OF OPS DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS
CHIEF EXEC OFFICER CEO
CHIEF OPERATING OFFICER COO
EXEC VP EXECUTIVE VICE PRESIDENT
SVP OF MARKETING SENIOR VICE PRESIDENT OF MARKETING
VP FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION VICE PRESIDENT OF FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION
VP OF HR VICE PRESIDENT OF HUMAN RESOURCES
GEN COUNSEL GENERAL COUNSEL
CHAIRMAN OF BOARD CHAIR OF BOARD
CHAIRPERSON CHAIR
BOARD PRES BOARD PRESIDENT
MGR IT MANAGER IT
DIR OF NURSING DIRECTOR OF NURSING

What it does 

standardize_spelling()
+- fix_spelling()
   +- fix_vice(), fix_executive(), fix_director(), fix_president(), ...   (about 50 fix_* routines)
   +- condense_abbreviations(), simplify_clevels()
   +- remove_trailing_conjunctions(), fix_of()
   +- spellcheck()   (hunspell)
  • Each fix_* routine handles one word family: fix_vice() turns VP, V.P., VICE-PRES and EVP into their full forms, fix_director() handles DIR, DIRS, DRCTR, and so on.
  • fix_of() inserts the implicit “of” between a title and its subject: VICE PRESIDENT FINANCE becomes VICE PRESIDENT OF FINANCE.
  • Unambiguous C-suite titles are condensed (CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER becomes CEO, CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER becomes CFO). Titles without a standard abbreviation stay spelled out.
  • spellcheck() suggests a dictionary spelling for a word no routine knows.

Assets

Asset Type Used for Load it with
possible.titles word list (package data) title words that can precede an implicit “of” data(possible.titles)
likely.subjects word list (package data) subjects that follow “of” (FINANCE, DEVELOPMENT, …) data(likely.subjects)
the fix_* routines R functions the abbreviation and spelling rules themselves ?fix_spelling, ?fix_vice, …
hunspell R package (Imports) the spell-check dictionary hunspell::dictionary("en_US") 
data(possible.titles)
head(possible.titles, 10)
#> [1] "VICE PRESIDENT" "DIRECTOR"       "CHAIR"          "DEAN"          
#> [5] "TRUSTEE"        "CEO"            "SECRETARY"      "MANAGER"       
#> [9] "MEMBER"
data(likely.subjects)
head(likely.subjects, 15)
#>  [1] "OPERATIONS"     "FINANCE"        "ADMINISTRATION" "MANAGEMENT"    
#>  [5] "EXHIBIT"        "PUBLICITY"      "ACTIVITIES"     "BUILDING"      
#>  [9] "EDUCATION"      "MARKETING"      "STRATEGY"       "SALES"         
#> [13] "ENSHRINEMENT"   "ADVANCEMENT"    "FUNDRAISING"

Try it 

fix_spelling("VP")                        # VICE PRESIDENT
#> [1] "VICE PRESIDENT"
fix_spelling("SR D MARKETING")            # SENIOR DIRECTOR OF MARKETING
#> [1] "SENIOR DIRECTOR OF MARKETING"
fix_spelling("SECY")                      # SECRETARY
#> [1] "SECRETARY"
fix_spelling("VICE PRESIDENT FINANCE")    # VICE PRESIDENT OF FINANCE
#> [1] "VICE PRESIDENT OF FINANCE"
fix_spelling("CHIEF EXEC OFFICER")        # CEO
#> [1] "CEO"
fix_spelling("CHIEF ADVANCEMENT OFFICER") # unchanged: no standard abbreviation
#> [1] "CHIEF ADVANCEMENT OFFICER"
fix_vice(c("EVP", "SVP", "V.P."))
#> [1] "EXECUTIVE VICE PRESIDENT" "SENIOR VICE PRESIDENT"   
#> [3] "V.P."

Input: TitleTxt4. Output: TitleTxt5, with standard spelling. Continue with step 06.
